after: ## Trade and commerce: why they are not the same word
alt: A tree. Commerce splits into trade and aids to trade. Trade divides into home trade (wholesale and retail) and international trade (exports and imports). The six aids to trade are communications, transport, warehousing, advertising, banking and insurance.
caption: Commerce is wider than trade: it adds the services that make trade possible.

alt: A textile firm in Pakistan sells towels to a buyer in Germany. Towels go one way and money comes back, so the sale is an export for Pakistan and an import for Germany. A foreign tourist paying for a hotel stay is buying an exported service.
caption: One transaction is an export for the seller’s country and an import for the buyer’s.

alt: Between producer and consumer stand six barriers, each removed by one aid to trade: no contact by communications, distance by transport, timing by warehousing, lack of awareness by advertising, payment and finance by banking, and fear of loss by insurance.
caption: Link each aid to the barrier it removes to turn a list into an explanation.

alt: The three elements of logistics: transport, freight forwarders and warehousing. A freight forwarder books space with carriers, combines small loads, prepares shipping documents and arranges customs clearance, often using other firms’ vehicles.
caption: Logistics manages transport, freight forwarding and warehousing together.

alt: Four checks on the evidence: a physical location means traditional commerce; buying through social media posts or messages means scommerce; using a mobile device such as the store’s own app means mcommerce; only “placed online” means ecommerce. Each has an example.
caption: Choose the most specific term that the evidence in the case supports.

after: ## Worked example: an annotated model answer
alt: Four linked steps, one mark each: the farm produces mangoes; it needs trade to sell them through wholesalers and retailers; trade needs aids such as refrigerated transport and insurance; and traders depend on the farm, so a failed harvest hits trade and commercial services.
caption: Each sentence makes a separate link, applied to the mango farm.
